framework.reasoning: The SIR's implementation_assumptions section (confidence 0.85) notes the authors released a PyTorch reference implementation (torchdiffeq) post-publication, which is the de facto community standard for reproducing this paper, even though the original 2018 experiments used Autograd + scipy.integrate + TensorFlow + Fortran solvers. PyTorch also gives first-class custom autograd.Function support, which is exactly what the adjoint sensitivity method (Eqs. 4-5, Algorithm 1/2) needs. CUDA is optional since the original experiments (MNIST, toy densities, 2D spirals) are small enough to run on CPU; GPU is offered as an option, not a requirement. Plain YAML is sufficient given the modest number of hyperparameter groups (no need for Hydra's multirun/compose features).

module_hierarchy.description: Training loop shared by ResNet/RK-Net/ODE-Net on MNIST; logs test error, param count, and NFE per epoch (reproducing Table 1 and Figure 3).
Two training modes: density-matching (minimize KL(q||p), Adam, 10k iters) and maximum-likelihood (train q on data, reverse for sampling), reproducing Section 4.1.
VAE training loop for the latent ODE model following Appendix E: encode -> sample z_t0 -> ODESolve -> decode -> maximize ELBO.
Loss functions: cross-entropy (classification), KL(q||p) (density matching), negative ELBO (latent ODE, Appendix E Eq. context), Poisson process log-likelihood (Section 5, optional extension).
Test error, predictive RMSE (Table 2), and NFE-vs-error tracking (Figure 3) used across the three experiment families.
YAML config loader/validator with dataclass-backed schema mirroring config_schema below.

tensor_flows.name: ODE-Net MNIST classification forward pass
steps: h0 = ConvDownsample(x)                          -> [B, C, 6, 6]  (TODO: verify exact spatial size from paper; ambiguity flagged in SIR)
h1 = ODEBlock(ConvODEFunc)(h0, t=[0,1])          -> [B, C, 6, 6]  (adjoint method computes gradients w.r.t. h0 and dynamics params without storing forward activations)

tensor_flows.name: Continuous Normalizing Flow forward (density -> sample or sample -> density)
steps: augmented_state1 = ODEBlock(PlanarCNFDynamics)(augmented_state0, t=[0,1]) -> [B, 3]  (dynamics returns both dz/dt and d(logp)/dt per Eq. 8-9)
logp_z1 = logp_z0 - delta_logp                                       -> [B, 1]  (sign per Eq. 6/8 change-of-variables convention)

tensor_flows.name: Latent ODE reconstruction + extrapolation
steps: z_traj = ODEBlock(LatentODEFunc)(z_t0, t=t_query)                    -> [M, B, 4]  (t_query spans both observed and extrapolated times, per Figure 6)

risk_assessment.description: MNIST classification hyperparameters (optimizer, learning rate, batch size, number of epochs) are not stated in the parsed paper text; Table 1 results (0.42% test error for ODE-Net) may not be exactly reproducible without the true settings.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Expose optimizer/LR/batch-size as config flags with the assumed defaults (Adam, 1e-3, 128) clearly marked ASSUMED in config.yaml; document in README that these are literature-standard guesses, and suggest a small grid search to match the reported 0.42% test error.

risk_assessment.description: The exact downsampling stem architecture (conv kernel/stride sizes) before the residual/ODE blocks is unspecified.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement ConvDownsample as a swappable module (config-driven kernel/stride list) defaulting to two stride-2 3x3 convs; add a unit test asserting the output spatial size matches whatever is configured, so alternate downsampling schemes can be tried without touching model code.

risk_assessment.description: Custom implementation of the adjoint sensitivity method (Appendix B/C) is mathematically intricate (augmented state, vector-Jacobian products, sign conventions for backward-time integration) and easy to get subtly wrong, which would silently corrupt gradients.
risk_assessment.source: SIR mathematical_spec entries for Eqs. 4-5 and Appendix B/C (confidence 0.95, but implementation is non-trivial)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Provide `TorchdiffeqAdaptiveSolver` (backed by the well-tested community `torchdiffeq` package) as the default/recommended backend, and keep the from-scratch `OdeintAdjointMethod` as an educational, well-unit-tested alternative validated via `torch.autograd.gradcheck` against direct backprop through a fixed-step solver on small examples.

risk_assessment.description: RNN cell type (vanilla/GRU/LSTM) for the latent ODE recognition network is unspecified.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Make `RecognitionRNN` accept a `cell_type` config flag (default GRU) so the choice is trivially swappable and testable against Table 2 RMSE numbers.

risk_assessment.description: Gaussian observation noise standard deviation for the synthetic spiral dataset is not given a numeric value in the parsed text.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Expose `spiral_observation_noise_std` as a config value (default 0.1) and treat it as a tunable reproduction parameter; document the assumption in the README and config comments.

risk_assessment.description: The synthetic spiral dataset is not publicly released, so exact reproduction of Table 2 numbers depends on regenerating data with matching statistical properties rather than loading an original file.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement `SpiralDataset` as a seeded generator (numpy RandomState) so results are at least internally reproducible run-to-run, and document that absolute RMSE values may differ slightly from the paper's Table 2 due to different random spiral instantiations.
